\chapter{Advice and hesitation}
\label{ch:ar-advice-and-hesitation}
\hlchaptermodality{369}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say that someone advised, hinted, encouraged or hesitated, and talk about an alternative.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 369: I can say that someone advised, hinted, encouraged or hesitated, and talk about an alternative.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{نصح} (naṣaḥa)}{نصح (naṣaḥa)}]{\ar{نصح} (naṣaḥa) — to advise}

\label{lesson:AR-C369-nasaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to neglect, then the Arabic for to care about.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{نصح}}
\textbf{\ar{نصح}} — \emph{naṣaḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}to advise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نصحني} \ar{الطبيب} \ar{بالراحة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{naṣaḥanī aṭ-ṭabīb bi-r-rāḥa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor advised me to rest.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينصح}, \emph{yanṣaḥ}.

The advice comes after \ar{بـ} or \ar{أن}: \ar{نصحه} \ar{بـ} …, \ar{نصحه} \ar{أن} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{نصح}} (\emph{naṣaḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-ṣ-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be sincere\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Naṣaḥa} is a Form I verb: to give sincere counsel, to advise.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naṣaḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naṣaḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{naṣaḥanī aṭ-ṭabīb bi-r-rāḥa.} — The doctor advised me to rest.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to neglect, then the Arabic for to care about, then say \emph{naṣaḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{نصح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To advise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لمح} (lammaḥa)}{لمح (lammaḥa)}]{\ar{لمح} (lammaḥa) — to hint}

\label{lesson:AR-C369-lammaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to care about, then the Arabic for to advise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لمح}}
\textbf{\ar{لمح}} — \emph{lammaḥa} — \textquotedblleft{}to hint\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لمح} \ar{المدير} \ar{إلى} \ar{تغيير} \ar{قريب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lammaḥa al-mudīr ilā taghyīr qarīb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager hinted at a change coming soon.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يلمح}, \emph{yulammiḥ}.

It takes \ar{إلى}: \ar{لمح} \ar{إلى} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لمح}} (\emph{lammaḥa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-m-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to glance\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to make someone catch a glance: to hint at a thing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lammaḥa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lammaḥa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lammaḥa al-mudīr ilā taghyīr qarīb.} — The manager hinted at a change coming soon.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to care about, then the Arabic for to advise, then say \emph{lammaḥa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{لمح} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hint\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شجع} (shajjaʿa)}{شجع (shajjaʿa)}]{\ar{شجع} (shajjaʿa) — to encourage}

\label{lesson:AR-C369-shajjaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to advise, then the Arabic for to hint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شجع}}
\textbf{\ar{شجع}} — \emph{shajjaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to encourage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شجعني} \ar{أبي} \ar{على} \ar{تعلم} \ar{الرسم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shajjaʿanī abī ʿalā taʿallum ar-rasm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father encouraged me to learn drawing.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشجع}, \emph{yushajjiʿ}.

It takes \ar{على}: \ar{شجعه} \ar{على} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شجع}} (\emph{shajjaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-j-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be brave\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to make brave: to encourage.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تردد} (taraddada)}{تردد (taraddada)}]{\ar{تردد} (taraddada) — to hesitate}

\label{lesson:AR-C369-taraddada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to hint, then the Arabic for to encourage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تردد}}
\textbf{\ar{تردد}} — \emph{taraddada} — \textquotedblleft{}to hesitate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تردد} \ar{الولد} \ar{قبل} \ar{أن} \ar{يقفز} \ar{في} \ar{الماء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taraddada al-walad qabla an yaqfiza fī al-māʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boy hesitated before jumping into the water.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتردد}, \emph{yataraddad}.

Also to go often: \ar{تردد} \ar{على} \ar{السوق}, went to the market often.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تردد}} (\emph{taraddada}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-d-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to send back\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form V, to turn back and forth: to waver, to hesitate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taraddada}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taraddada}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taraddada al-walad qabla an yaqfiza fī al-māʾ.} — The boy hesitated before jumping into the water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to hint, then the Arabic for to encourage, then say \emph{taraddada} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تردد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hesitate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بديل} (badīl)}{بديل (badīl)}]{\ar{بديل} (badīl) — an alternative}

\label{lesson:AR-C369-badil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to encourage, then the Arabic for to hesitate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بديل}}
\textbf{\ar{بديل}} — \emph{badīl} — \textquotedblleft{}an alternative\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{الدراجة} \ar{بديل} \ar{جيد} \ar{عن} \ar{السيارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ad-darrāja badīl jayyid ʿan as-sayyāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A bicycle is a good alternative to a car.
\end{quote}

\ar{بديل} \ar{عن} or \ar{بديل} \ar{لـ}: an alternative to.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بديل}} (\emph{badīl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{b-d-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to change, to put in place of\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A \emph{badīl} is what is put in place of another: a substitute, an alternative.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badīl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badīl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ad-darrāja badīl jayyid ʿan as-sayyāra.} — A bicycle is a good alternative to a car.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to encourage, then the Arabic for to hesitate, then say \emph{badīl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بديل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An alternative\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
